clue.text: British fish and others around for shopping

indicators.note: the Latin phrase for others goes round the fish, holding it inside

parts.note: et al. is Latin shorthand for 'and others'
a ray is a flat cartilaginous fish

explanation.surface: A list of British fish and other goods bought on a trip to the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shopping' here is the slang sense of informing on someone to the police, not buying groceries.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopping someone is slang for grassing on them, an act of treachery or disloyalty.

clue.text: Composer embracing cold American god

indicators.note: the composer's name holds the letter for cold within it, like a hug

parts.note: J. S. Bach is the German composer
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A composer hugging a chilly American deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchus is the Roman deity of wine and revelry, so he is a god.

clue.text: Light meal Athena regularly provides

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the goddess's name, at regular intervals, from the second on

explanation.surface: The goddess Athena reliably supplies a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Afternoon tea is a small meal of sandwiches and cake taken around four o'clock in Britain.

clue.text: Transport gold fabric clothing gang

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: the fabric wraps around the gang as clothes cover a body

parts.note: toile is a light linen or cotton fabric
a mob is a gang of criminals

explanation.surface: A gang dressed in golden fabric is being transported.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is a means of transport, and automobile is the formal or American word for one.

clue.text: Somewhat embarrassing 16

definitions.note: the solution to 16 down, a woven wall hanging

indicators.note: only part of the word embarrassing is wanted, the letters sitting within it

explanation.surface: Something at 16 is a bit embarrassing.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 down is TAPESTRY; an arras is a tapestry hanging, named after the French town of Arras.
explanation.definitionFit: An arras is a rich woven wall hanging, a kind of tapestry, behind which Polonius famously hid.

clue.text: Church to copy Lutyens' façade in religious building

parts.note: to ape is to imitate or copy

indicators.note: a façade is the front face of a building, so the opening letter of the architect's name

explanation.surface: A church imitating the front of a Lutyens building, the architect being Sir Edwin Lutyens.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small place of worship, often part of a larger church or college.

clue.text: No end to dismal accommodation in resort

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for wretched housing is cut off

parts.note: a hovel is a squalid, wretched dwelling

explanation.surface: Endless gloomy lodgings at a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hove is a seaside town in Sussex, next to Brighton on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Hove is an English seaside town, a holiday spot in the sense of a resort.

clue.text: Men feature in virgin's paintings

indicators.note: the soldiers and the feature are placed within the word for virginal

parts.note: virgin is, in the sense of being pure and untouched
OR, other ranks, is crossword shorthand for soldiers who are not officers
a trait is a distinguishing feature

explanation.surface: Male figures appearing in a series of pictures of the Virgin Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: Portraiture is the art of painting likenesses, used collectively for portraits as a body of work.

clue.text: Rest of weight porky lecturer carries

parts.note: porky (pork pie) is British rhyming slang for a lie

indicators.note: the lecturer holds the weight inside him

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: An overweight lecturer carrying the rest of the weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porky' looks like it describes the lecturer; it is rhyming slang, porky pie for lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-down is a short nap or repose, so it is a rest.

clue.text: In meantime firm must replace current phone system

indicators.note: the company abbreviation goes in where the current symbol was

parts.note: in the interim means in the meantime
I is the physics symbol for electric current
CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Meanwhile a company has to swap out the electricity supply for a telephone network.
explanation.definitionFit: An intercom is an internal telephone or speaker network within a building.

clue.text: Local branch hostile about new detailed references

parts.note: a chapter is a local branch of a society or club

indicators.note: the word for hostile goes round the abbreviation for new

parts.note: adverse means unfavourable or hostile

explanation.surface: A local branch is unfriendly towards new, detailed citations.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving chapter and verse means citing the exact source, an idiom from Bible references.

clue.text: Senior instructor getting post in footer? The opposite!

indicators.note: the post is placed within the opposite of footer

parts.note: the reverse of a footer, a text strip at the page bottom, is a header at the top
a mast is a tall upright post

explanation.surface: A senior teacher getting a job in football, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Footer' is British slang for football and 'post' suggests a job, but footer's opposite is a header and the post is a mast.
explanation.definitionFit: The head teacher of a school is its most senior instructor.

clue.text: Bet one will be put on charge

definitions.meaning: a multiple wager in which winnings from each race roll on to the next

definitions.text: one will be put on charge
definitions.meaning: a rechargeable battery that stores electricity, as plugged in to charge

explanation.surface: A wager that someone will be arrested and charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on charge' suggests an arrest; the second sense is a storage battery being recharged.
explanation.definitionFit: In British betting a multiple bet rolling winnings forward, and also an old word for a rechargeable storage battery.

clue.text: Tactic initially used by City Group

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word tactic is wanted

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city, often shortened to Rio

explanation.surface: A tactic first deployed by a city football side.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three, such as a three-piece band.

clue.text: Destruction of Capitol occurring in month? This could spread!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit within the month abbreviation

parts.note: APR is the abbreviation for April

indicators.note: the word Capitol is wrecked so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An attack on the US Capitol in a given month might spread, like unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole final sentence: 'This could spread!' describes a tool, not the riot in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An applicator is a tool for spreading or applying a substance such as glue or cream.

clue.text: Dismiss objection showing old-fashioned brass

parts.note: to sack is to fire someone from a job
a but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Firing someone over a complaint reveals old-fashioned money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' looks like slang for money or for senior officers; here it is a brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is an early form of trombone, a Renaissance brass instrument.

clue.text: Design such as Odo commissioned records shot

parts.note: tapes are recordings
a shot is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A design of the kind Bishop Odo ordered captures a shot on record.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishop Odo of Bayeux is thought to have commissioned the Bayeux Tapestry, depicting the Norman conquest of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bayeux embroidery, ordered by Odo, is the most famous example of a woven pictorial hanging.

clue.text: Top individual appearing in fashion title

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the word for fashion

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or style, as in bon ton
I, the single person, as one individual

explanation.surface: A leading figure features in a fashion headline.
explanation.definitionFit: A caption is a heading or descriptive title beside a picture.

clue.text: Gucci to start with simply formed tunic

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the fashion house name is taken
the letters of simply are formed into a new shape

explanation.surface: Gucci, for a start, simply designed a tunic.
explanation.walkthrough: A gymslip is a sleeveless tunic once worn as British school uniform for girls.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymslip is a sleeveless pinafore tunic, formerly part of girls' school uniform.

clue.text: Terribly urgent cases hard for this German

indicators.note: the rearranged letters encase the hard letter
urgent is mangled badly, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Desperate cases are hard for this particular German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' scrambles URGENT into GUNTER; 'cases' wraps that round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunther is a German male name, borne by the Gibichung king in Wagner's Ring cycle.

clue.text: Spineless creature welcomes us to Flanders clubs

indicators.note: the heroine's name and the suit letter take in the word us

parts.note: Moll Flanders, Defoe's heroine, so Moll is the name that goes before Flanders
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Cowardly Flanders golf clubs invite us in, a weak, spineless bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to Flanders' means the word placed before Flanders: Moll, from Daniel Defoe's novel Moll Flanders.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails, clams and octopuses have no backbone, so this invertebrate is a creature without a spine.

clue.text: Fanciful idea concerning church in short quote

indicators.note: about plus church are placed within the shortened quote
the word for quote is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to cite is to quote
on means about or concerning
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A whimsical notion about the church inside a brief quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceit is an elaborate or fanciful notion, especially an extended metaphor in poetry.

clue.text: Long-distance runner having zero energy

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A marathon runner who has no energy left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete; it is a river that runs a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: The great African river is the world's longest, so it runs for a very long distance.

clue.text: Shield lets axe in once and he's crocked

indicators.note: the word for axe is let into the rearranged letters
crocked means injured or broken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it

explanation.surface: A shield admits an axe once, and he is injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lets' only joins: the word 'in' is what places the axe synonym inside the rearranged pool.
explanation.definitionFit: An escutcheon is the shield-shaped surface on which a coat of arms is displayed in heraldry.

clue.text: Motivates writer to dispense with peripheral characters

indicators.note: the novelist's name loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Anthony Burgess, author of A Clockwork Orange

explanation.surface: Encourages a novelist to drop minor characters from the book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peripheral characters' looks like minor figures in a novel; it means the outer letters of the writer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone is to drive or push them on, so it motivates them.

clue.text: Greeting in place for little man

indicators.note: the greeting goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place in addresses
hi is a casual greeting

explanation.surface: Saying hello somewhere to a small boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little man' means a man's name in short form: Phil is short for Philip.
explanation.definitionFit: A diminutive of Philip, this is a shortened male name, hence a man in little.

clue.text: Affect Tory supporters with reminder to behave appropriately

parts.note: to hit is to affect badly, as in 'hit by the cuts'
the right are the conservative wing of politics
a note is a memo or reminder

explanation.surface: Hurt the Conservatives' backers with a prompt to mind their manners.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike the correct tone is to say or do just the right thing for the occasion.

clue.text: Lyric poem's style devoid of metre?

definitions.note: lyric poem is, the 's standing for is

indicators.note: the style word loses the abbreviation for metre

parts.note: a mode is a style or manner

explanation.surface: Is a lyric verse's style without regular rhythm?
explanation.walkthrough: 'metre' looks like poetic rhythm; it is the unit of length, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyrical poem addressed to a subject, often in elevated style.

clue.text: Margins deserting Arab Bank? Not often!

indicators.note: the outer letters leave the word Arab, keeping the inner pair

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: Profit margins abandoning an Arab bank, which is seldom seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means seldom, on few occasions.

clue.text: Greedy — backing stratagem, that is — not heartless

indicators.note: the trick word is read backwards

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or stratagem
i.e., id est, means that is

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word not is removed, keeping its outsides

explanation.surface: Greedy support for a scheme, that is, though not heartless.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient is a literary word for hungry or ravenous, hence greedy.
